The finding

The question

Gemma-3-12B-IT refuses more often when a prompt is in Slovene. Is it better at spotting harm in Slovene, or does it simply say no more often?

The answer

It says no more often. On the 1,093 benign prompts of the HARD set, unedited Gemma refuses of the Slovene versions and of the English ones, 1.56 times as often. GaMS3, built on the same Gemma-3 base with Slovene training, refuses in both languages.

splits a refusal rate into two parts: , how well the model separates harmful from benign prompts, and the , where it puts its threshold. The model-by-language interaction sits in the criterion:

      Where it fails

      Which analysis choices keep the effect, and which break it?

      Measure

      What the paper does not show

      • The headline is an ESTIMATE. DiDc reverses to −0.31 [−0.62, −0.09] when partial answers are coded as refusals, so the coding rule decides whether the over-refusal is attributed to Gemma at all.
      • No judge was validated against humans. The Qwen3-14B judge was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV (binary κ 0.68–0.86). On edited rows no judge exceeds κ = 0.51 against blind adjudication, and that adjudication is by an author-model LLM, not a person. The readout gate never passed.
      • One sample. The Qwen3-14B rescoring interval [0.39, 0.67] re-derives the same Experiment 5 items; it is not an independent sample. On edited models the criterion difference is 0.14 [−0.78, 1.12], consistent with zero.
      • The reply-language effect has a weak anchor. Experiment 16 gives OUTGemma = +2.43 [+0.89, +5.38] after PPI correction, but the harmful-content adjudicator κ is 0.12 against a 0.60 gate.
      • GaMS3 ignored the reply-language instruction off the English-prompt row (SL→EN compliance 0.00), so GaMS3 mechanism claims are limited to that row.
      • Hungarian is uninformative (minimum detectable effect about 3 log-odds), both models ran in 4-bit NF4, Slovene prompts are machine translations with no native-speaker check, and the benign false-refusal adjudication has only 30 items per cell.
      • Novelty is partial. Language-dependent over-refusal is anticipated by Addagada (2026) and Nguyen et al. (2026); the contribution here is the signal-detection split and the sibling-pair design.
